utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Before we hear the next witness, there is a housekeeping matter I would like to deal with. On the 25th September, 2003, the Prosecution submitted a written request for the certification of an interlocutory appeal concerning of the evidence in the Jokic case. After deliberations of this Bench, we believe that the certification is not warranted for several reasons. Basically, it boils down to reliability. Firstly, the Prosecution accepts that the information obtained through suspect interviews is unreliable, particularly when compared with other sources of evidence, such as direct testimony and especially in view of the fact the suspects need not make a solemn declaration. Secondly, as the Prosecution itself stresses, the information obtained will only be one part of his case and therefore of corroborating value rather than anything else. As rightly and already held by the Trial Chamber, the unreliability of information from suspects makes such evidence weigh very lightly in the overall web of a party's evidence. Thirdly, any prevarication bears suspect because it's difficult to establish either objectively prima facie in the middle of a case without having heard or seen any of the other party's evidence of the matter, and certainly because the unreliability of evidence is purely speculative. And only as to the unreliability of the evidence. Fourthly, lastly, considering the above, the evidence therefore does not reach the level of the significance required by the Rule 73(B). It does not involve an issue that would significantly affect the fair and expeditious conduct of the proceedings or the outcome of the trial. And that, in the Trial Chamber's opinion, an immediate resolution by the Appeals Chamber will not materially advance the proceedings. Therefore, the certification requested by the Prosecution is therefore denied. It is so decided. Are there any other matters that the parties would like to bring to the attention of this Trial Chamber at this stage? Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, Mr. President. I just wanted to give the Court a brief idea of this week. We appreciate the Court and counsel agreeing for another few witnesses. And I know the RS and the OTP has worked hard to make those witnesses available. And in fact, we do have the first two that are all ready to go. And we have a third that we hope to have on Friday. It's looking good that he will be able to show. It's, again, a matter of visas and these sorts of things and it's looking good. And I would also like to alert the Court to one last potential witness that we have just come across that we may try to squeeze in on Thursday, if the Court is amenable. I've filed some papers in that regard that is coming, so you can take a look at it and do of course whatever you choose. And it is a personal security person for Mr. Blagojevic that has some, I think, very important information to provide base -- on both sides of the case, actually. It should be very short. We're not sure if logistically we can make it. But, as I say, last, I promise, last we want to end this, as you know. But we're going to try to do it logistically. And I just would ask you to look at the papers and we can, of course -- we'll be here for your -- any comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm surprised to hear that the list is growing. I suspected the last day of the Prosecution's case very soon, otherwise all the proceedings have to be postponed. At this stage could I hear from the Defence. Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours. It's good to be back. Frankly, I'm not disappointed that they're going to bring in this additional witness. He's extremely exculpatory in our case. I think it -- he should be helpful to Your Honours. And in fact, as I have indicated on the record and I have indicated to Mr. McCloskey's colleague, We welcome as many witnesses as they can drag up because they won't find anything that will tie Mr. Blagojevic into any of the atrocities. And I understand right now they're in a process of interviewing cleaning ladies and people that made coffee and what have you down in Bratunac, so we don't care. But we'll be ready, willing, and able to meet these other witnesses on Thursday and on Friday. I just would like to remind everybody that Mr. Blagojevic does have a family visit the following week, and so I certainly do not want for any witnesses to drag on to the following week. If we can avoid that. And if the Prosecution intends to bring on additional witnesses, that they do so after Mr. Blagojevic's family visit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think this Bench will make decisions when we receive any written submissions from the Prosecution, but as a principle we hope that the Prosecution's case will draw to an end as soon as possible, because according to our time schedule if we have any delay, everything has to be delayed, especially for the 98 bis filings by the Defence. Well, having said that, could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration according to the paper the usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Shin, your direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Thank you, Mr. Usher, for moving that aside.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell the Trial Chamber your full name?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Milan Nedjelkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Just so it's clear on the record, could you please spell your last name.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: N-e-d-e-l-j-k-o-v-i-c [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, when were you born?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: 1st of June, 1957.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And where was that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: In Sikirici, Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm just going to ask you a few questions now about your background. Could you tell us briefly your education?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I am a car mechanic and a driver by occupation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: What year did you finish high school?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And what did you do after high school?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I took a job at Sase Srebrenica mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And when did you begin working there?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Would you please just explain briefly what your job was.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: About six months I worked as a car mechanic. And after that for the whole time, I worked as a driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Were you still working as a driver at the beginning of the war in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Were you mobilised at some point during the war?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: During the war from 1992 until September, I had a work obligation at the mine -- or rather until October 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And what happened in October 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: In October of 1992, did you -- did you change your work? Did you do something different?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I also worked as a driver at the mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Were you at some point mobilised by the army?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: In 1994 -- before 1994, or rather, towards the end of August or early September I was again mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And what unit were you mobilised into?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did you have a rank?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I was just an ordinary soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And what was your -- what kind of job did you have as a regular soldier?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I kept guard on the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And I'm sorry. Just so that the record is clear, this was end of August, early September, in 1994. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did at some point your job change from being a guard to something else?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: In late January 1995, I was reassigned to the brigade command as a driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And when you say "brigade," do I understand you to mean the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: How many drivers were there at the Bratunac Brigade command?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: At the time there were three of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Can you tell us who the other two people were, please.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Savo Jovanovic and Pero, I also think that his last name was Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Would all three of you be on duty at the same time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: No. We took shifts. Two were on duty and one was off-duty. That was the usual procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, could you please tell us what the name of your superior officer was when you were driver at the command of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Milomir Stanojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Could you tell us his rank or his position.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if he had any rank, but he was a headquarters commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nedjelkovic, I'd like to take you now to the day of the fall of Srebrenica. And I'd like to ask you first: Where were you on the morning that Srebrenica fell?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I was in Bratunac on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And where in Bratunac were you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: At the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Were you on duty that day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I think I was. Yeah, I'm sure I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: How was it that you learned that Srebrenica had fallen on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I heard it on the radio in the afternoon when I went home for lunch, and that's when I heard that Srebrenica had fallen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did you leave Bratunac Brigade command during that day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: On that day?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you remember who the other driver was on duty that day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Pero should have been on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And where was Pero during that day, as far as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I do not know. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If I could just have a moment, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, do you recall that we - you and I and an investigator from the Prosecution office - met yesterday to review your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. Just one moment, please. I'd like to refer to you -- I'd like to refer you to some notes that were taken of our discussion yesterday to see if that might help refresh your memory. Just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would like the Prosecutor to first ask the gentleman to repeat here in court if he recalls what he said yesterday, before trying to refresh his memory or impeach him with any documents that were generated by their investigator. Unless they're going to produce a tape-recording so the gentleman can hear himself on the tape. So if he could just first ask him what he remembers saying yesterday with respect to this line of questioning before going to any documents. Again, as I repeatedly have complained in this case, the proofing notes are always done, they're rough notes taken by an investigator, and there's no way for this gentleman to verify exactly what he has said if it hasn't been recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I believe Mr. Shin will ask that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, if you could, could you recall what you told me and Mr. Alistair Graham, the investigator, what you told us yesterday about where the other driver was on the day that Srebrenica fell. Can you recall that now?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: One of the drivers was with the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know where the driver and the commander were on the day that Srebrenica fell?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I suppose they were at Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And why do you think that they were at Pribicevac on that day? I'm sorry, maybe that didn't come through clearly to the witness. The question was: Could you just explain to us --

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. I'll be happy to repeat it. Why is it that you think that the other driver and the commander were at Pribicevac on the day that Srebrenica fell?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: They were there at Pribicevac while Srebrenica was going on, but I don't know why they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are we talking about the 11th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I believe the witness's testimony is that this is the day Srebrenica fell, and he knows that because he heard it on the radio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I just want to make sure that we're talking about the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm told there may be a correction on the translation. The gentleman indicated where they were, not why they were. I believe that's what he indicated, and I think it's on line --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If I may, it may have something to do with the form of my question, but I believe that was responsive to my question since I was merely asking him why he -- basically what the basis was for him to think they were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you could re-ask this question to see how the witness is going to tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, just for clarification, if you could, could you please explain the basis you have for -- the grounds for which -- simply the reason why you believed that the other driver and the commander were up in Pribicevac on the day that Srebrenica fell.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I can tell for myself where I was, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: But if I understand your evidence then, as far as you know the other driver --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Now he's asking the witness to speculate. The witness testified that he doesn't know. He knows about his own whereabouts. He indicated that he suspected that they were up in Pribicevac. Now he's trying to get a confirmation. So I would appreciate that we move on. The question has been asked and it has been answered in more than one way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we believe so. The witness has answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. I'll certainly move on then, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, at the end of the day that -- on that day that Srebrenica fell in the evening, did you see the other driver return to the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I saw Savo when he returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Was Savo the driver who was on duty that day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And just to be clear on the record, I believe you had said earlier that Pero was the man who was on -- who was the other duty driver that day. Was it Savo or was it Pero?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps both of them. I cannot remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: When you saw Savo returning to the headquarters, do you recall if the commander was with him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I suppose that he came back with him in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Nedjelkovic, I'd like you to take you now to the next day. This is -- we're going to be talking now about the day after the fall of Srebrenica. Where were you in the morning of that day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I was at the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: What time did you get there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Normally at around 7.00 or quarter to 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: When did you leave the brigade command?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't say exactly. I poured fuel into the tank of my vehicle. I had coffee, so maybe half an hour later I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And who did you leave with?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I drove commander Blagojevic and Savo Cvjetinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. And just before we continue on that, one point of clarification. When you spoke about the commander on the previous day, the day that Srebrenica fell, you were also speaking of Commander Blagojevic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Were you told where you should go when these two gentlemen got into the car?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I said that we were going towards Sase and Zalazje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did somebody tell you to go in that direction?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And just so that we're clear, did you pick up Mr. Blagojevic and Mr. Cvjetinovic? Did they get into your car at the brigade command or did you pick them up somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember now exactly, but I think it was near the command headquarters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. At this point, I know it's a little technical, but the question was leading in nature. And I think we're getting -- this is kind of sensitive. He could have asked him, Where did you pick them up? So now that -- and as a result of the question being suggestive, we got the answer we which got because the gentleman doesn't recall exactly. I would appreciate -- I know that the gentleman is trying to do a good job, but I would appreciate if there were no leading questions as we inch along this particular line of questioning, because it is rather important, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, is that an important issue, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. I believe if it wasn't they wouldn't be asking the question, number one. Obviously they're trying to figure out where was Mr. Blagojevic and where they picked him up because they're trying to tie him in somehow to meetings, places where others were involved. So -- but in essence what I would like -- I don't know -- down the road whether we're going to be in a sensitive area, and I certainly don't want at this point to let go of this opportunity to point out to my colleague on the other end that I would appreciate him asking open-ended questions: Who, what, when, where, why, how, and explain, as opposed to saying: Did you pick them up at the brigade command, which is suggestive in nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But the answer of this witness does not seem to me that he was led by the Prosecution. He just said that he did not remember now exactly. But it's near the commander's headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well -- and my -- Ms. Tomanovic tells me that perhaps there was a mishap in the translation, so if the question could be asked again. I don't want to suggest what he might have said, you know. But ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But we believe that we have to trust the interpretations of this Tribunal. Maybe there is a small nuances there. In this way, since you raise this issued, Mr. Shin, would you please repeat your question and try your best to give open-ended questions to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, on this morning, the day after the fall of Srebrenica, where was it that Mr. Blagojevic and Mr. Cvjetinovic got into your car?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, but I think it took place in front of the command headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, you mentioned that someone told you to go in the direction of Sase and Zalazje. Could you please tell us who it was that told you to go in that direction?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: The people who were in the car instructed me which direction to take.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Was there anyone in the car, apart from Mr. Blagojevic and Mr. Cvjetinovic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did they both tell you, or was it one of them?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I suppose one of them. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you recall which one of the two it was?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, I had asked you earlier what time this was. Perhaps you could help us by telling us whether it was before noon or after noon when you left the brigade headquarters, just so that we're clear.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: In the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know who -- I'm sorry. Let me rephrase that. Mr. Nedjelkovic, who was Mr. Cvjetinovic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Savo Cvjetinovic, he was an officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Which unit was he an officer in?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I hadn't known him from before, before he came to the Bratunac Brigade. And after that, he was at the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: When did he arrive at the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot tell you. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: What was his rank, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: He had a rank, but I cannot remember which rank it was when he came.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, you had explained that you were heading towards Sase and Zalazje. We have a map --

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: We have a map here if you could first explain to us in words the itinerary you took when you started heading in that direction. Could you please tell us what road -- well, first of all, where was the first place you stopped?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: First we went to Bratunac, Sase, and Zalazje. At Zalazje we stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. When you got to Zalazje and you stopped, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I had a flat tire on the road, so I had to change it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: What did Mr. Blagojevic and Mr. Cvjetinovic do?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: They just inspected the troops there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Which troops were they?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Was it any specific unit of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: How long was it that you stayed in Zalazje?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember. I didn't look at my watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And where did you go after Zalazje?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: We went down to the Srebrenica playground.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And when you say "we," do you mean all three of you or ...

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I think all three.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: When you got to the Srebrenica playground, did you stop there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: We stopped there. We also inspected the troops there and then returned up to Zalazje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And was it all three of you who returned up to Zalazje?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. All three of us headed for Zanik and Likare, beyond Zalazje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did you stop at Zanik and Likare?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: We got stuck there in the mud.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Where was the next place that you stopped?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: When we returned, we proceeded via Srebrenica towards Jadar and Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, just to be clear, when you were in the area of Zanik and Likare, apart from being stuck in the mud did you make a stop anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah, we stopped somewhere in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And what did you do when you stopped there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: They inspected the troops. That was where the troops were positioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: When you say "they," you mean Mr. Blagojevic and Mr. Cvjetinovic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you know which troops those were?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: The 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, I'm sorry I interrupted you. You had explained that you were proceeding via Srebrenica towards Jadar and Pribicevac. Where did you stop next?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Pribicevac. But before Pribicevac we didn't stop anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. What did you do when you stopped at Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: We arrived at Pribicevac. It was already dark and the lights were on. We inspected the troops, the logistics troops, and then we went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Were there any other troops there at Pribicevac when you stopped there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I think it was just the logistics troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: What were the logistics troops there doing?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: The command of the 3rd Battalion was there prior to the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And what was it -- when you had stopped in Pribicevac, what was it that the logistics drops -- I'm sorry, the logistics troops were doing?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: They were loading food items and other things they had there. They were loading it into the trucks and packing, kitchen equipment and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Were there any other troops -- I'm sorry. Just one --

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall how long it was you stayed in Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't say. It was dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: When you left Pribicevac, which direction did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: We took the road through Dimnici and went to Sase.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did you stop in Sase?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Where was the next place you stopped?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Sase and then on to Bijelovac and then we came to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And where in Bratunac did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: We went to the brigade headquarters I think. I parked the vehicle there. It was quite late.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: When you got to brigade headquarters, were Mr. Blagojevic and Mr. Cvjetinovic both still with you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I think they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And where did you leave Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I parked the vehicle there and went to sleep. I think the commander also went to bed. It was quite late.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Were there any other officers at the command headquarters when you got there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall. It was quite late. I didn't go inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Before you think the -- you mentioned that the commander, you think, also went to bed. Before that, did you notice that he went anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. What do you mean "before"?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: After you left -- after Mr. Blagojevic got out of your car at the brigade headquarters, did you -- did he go anywhere else that you saw?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, I'd like you to just take a look at the map that's on the bulletin board to your left. Sorry, it's on your left. Could you just explain to us briefly what that map shows.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Shall I get up?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honours, this is -- this map is marked P768.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, if you could just please explain to us what the red line on there is and what the numbers mean.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: This is the road we took.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And could you mark -- could you point to number 1 and explain what that is.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Zalazje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And was that the place where you explained you stopped the first time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If you could continue -- if you could please continue on. On the red line showing the path that you took, could you go to your second stop.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Number 2 is the playground of the sports field, that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And if you could just follow along the red line to show where you made your third stop.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we said that number 3 could be here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You -- did you say that number 3 would be there? Is that what you said? I'm not sure if the translation was correct there.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Number 3, yes, yes, yes. So that part after Zalazje is number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. And then could you please follow along the path that you took to get to your next stop.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: So we returned via Srebrenica. And then we went up to Jadar, Bukov Glava, and Pribicevac, which is number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And then if you could follow again on that map to show us your next stop.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: We took this road to go back towards Bratunac, as far as I remember. We went back to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: There's markings on there, are those markings you made, Mr. Nedjelkovic, the red line and the numbers?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the road we took, yes, yes. We marked that yesterday with you, approximately the road that we took.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And is that your signature on the left-hand side of that map?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay thank you. Yes, please. Mr. Nedjelkovic, when you had explained it was dark when you were at Pribicevac --

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: -- do you recall what time it was that you got back to the brigade headquarters in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: It had to be after 10.00 because it normally gets dark in our area at 8.00 or 8.30, and we would normally need at least two hours to get to Bratunac. So it had to be after 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: When you explained -- when we spoke yesterday you mentioned that it would have been about that time. Do you recall what you told -- do you recall what you told the investigators -- I'm sorry. Let me rephrase that. Do you recall when you gave a statement to investigators from the Prosecution on the 24th of January of this year?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'll repeat. Do you remember that you gave a statement to investigators from the Office of the Prosecutor in -- on the 24th of January of this year?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I do. I remember that I could tell that we left Pribicevac when there was -- when it was still -- I remember that when we left Pribicevac, my lights on the vehicle were on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you recall -- do you recall what you told the investigators about the -- about the approximate time when you arrived at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, I'd like to refer you to the transcript of that statement. And I'm going to refer you on the B/C/S version to page 5, line 27, to the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could someone please assist -- Mr. Usher, if you could please assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And I'd like you to read page 5 from line 27 to the bottom. And then on the following page, on page 6, from line 1 to line 9. If you could please read that to yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the English reference would be page 8, lines 1 through 16 -- I'm sorry, lines 1 through 14.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says here from between 9.00 until 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you recall saying that to the investigators then?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- interject here. I think if you look at a close reading of the transcript, they are asking: "Did you remain on duty that night?" And the answer is: "I was usually staying until 9.00 or 10.00. It depends on."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, it doesn't say -- he's saying generally that was his shift. Unfortunately we don't have then a follow-up question because probably the investigator was happy with what he heard or wasn't particularly listening, but on that -- he should have followed up by saying: On that particular night do you recall what time you knocked off. So I think they're trying to improperly impeach the witness with this segment. Secondly, I would suspect that they gave the gentleman an opportunity yesterday to read this statement that they have in B/C/S, and so when he did give an answer to which is recorded in their proofing notes, that it was sometime around 10.00 p.m., that they would have given him on opportunity to give an explanation. So I would object to this portion of his testimony -- of his transcript from his statement being used as a form of impeachment, because it is taken out of context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that the Prosecutor has finished with his question yet. Let me -- let us wait. You may proceed, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I was merely trying to see if that refreshed his memory as to the time that he returned to the brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, just one final question on that. There's a reference to your interview, the interview transcript. Does that refresh your recollection more precisely as to what time you returned to the Bratunac Brigade headquarters on that evening?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if we left Pribicevac when the lights on my car were on, that means that it was after 8.00. And I normally would need at least two hours to get to Bratunac, so it had to be after 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: And I stated there that normally I would stay that long when I was not on duty. Then I would stay until that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Nedjelkovic. I'd like to take you now to the following day. This is now two days after the fall of Srebrenica. Were you on duty that day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: That day -- on that day I was at the headquarters in the morning. I went to the car shop to fix the tyre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Blagojevic on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I know that his mother was ill around that time, and I think that somebody was supposed to drive him to the doctor's. But I didn't go because I was in the car shop. I don't know who else -- who went.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Just to be clear, my question was whether you saw Mr. Blagojevic on that day. I'm sorry, was there an answer?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see -- did you see -- do you know where Mr. Blagojevic -- I'm sorry. Do you know where Mr. Blagojevic's mother was? You said that she was ill.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: In Krasno Polje, at home. I heard that somebody told me that they drove the doctor in a car. Some people from our headquarters took the doctor down there. This is what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. On that day did you see -- did you leave the Bratunac Brigade headquarters, apart from fixing those things that you mentioned earlier?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did you see any officers at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters that day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I saw a lot of officers from elsewhere whom I didn't know at around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Were there any officers you recognised?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: During those days I saw General Krstic. I knew him because he was the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Was there anyone else that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did you drive Mr. Blagojevic anywhere on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Which day?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: On that specific day, two days after the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you remember when the next time you did drive Mr. Blagojevic was?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I remember before the commander went to Zepa we went to the bauxite mine in Podravanje for him to tour that area. There was a unit of ours there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And if I could just go through that with you. You mentioned that this was before Mr. Blagojevic went to Zepa. Do you recall how long it was after the fall of Srebrenica, this day that you're -- this trip that you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't remember the date, truly, but it was before the departure of the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: But after the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: After the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you recall where it was that you picked up Mr. Blagojevic for that trip?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was at the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: What time of day was that, as far as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: It was daylight, sometime after the morning. Now, whether it was before noon or not, I couldn't tell. I couldn't tell you what time it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Was it only Mr. Blagojevic you picked up? Was there someone else?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: One of the escorts came with us. I think it was Dragan.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If you can recall, what was this person's last name?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Just a minute. I think it was Ilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And what unit was this person from?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: He was with the headquarters, same unit as we were in. He was an escort.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: When you say the same unit, do you mean the Bratunac Brigade then?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. Which road did you take? You said you were going to the bauxite mines. Which road did you take in that direction?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: There are two routes. One went through Milici, and the other one through Srebrenica, Podravanje, and Gunja. I think that we used both of them. That's what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And you mentioned that you had -- that there was a unit there. What unit was that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: There were some troops from the Bratunac Brigade there at the positions towards Zepa near the bauxite mine. I think they were defending the mine, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: What did you do when you got to the bauxite mine?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: We went back to Gunja, which is where the bauxite mine is. The commander toured the troops and then we went on up there to tour some other troops, and then we went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: When you say you went on, could you tell us please where it was that you went on to.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Towards Podravanje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And is that where it was that -- well, what did you do when you got to Podravanje?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: There were troops deployed there. There was a line there of some sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And what did Mr. Blagojevic do when you got there to Podravanje?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: He was there talking to the troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: What did Mr. Ilic do when you were there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Ilic was there as a security person.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did he leave the car then and -- did he leave the car then?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And did he go with Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether he went with him and how far.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: You said that after you stopped in Podravanje, then you went back. Where was it that you went back to?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: We went back to the brigade in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Is that -- and where was it that you left Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I think at the brigade headquarters, but I'm not positive. I think it was at the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Was Mr. Ilic with you as well when you returned to the brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Most likely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately what time it was when you returned to the brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you recall if it was before noon or after noon?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: After noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, I'd like you to take a look at the second map up there on your left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this map is marked P767. It's a version of a map that was previously admitted as P671. This has some markings on it. Thank you, Mr. Usher. We seem to have a logistical problem up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, it's -- do you recall that I showed you this map yesterday when we met and do you recall that I asked you to make some marks on it indicating the routes you had taken to the bauxite mines? Could you please explain -- oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Could you please explain what the red lines are, the lines drawn in red marker.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: The two routes that one could take.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And if you could just please briefly explain both of those routes from the -- from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Bratunac, Konjevic Polje, Milici, and this is where Gunja is, the bauxite mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And you're pointing to number 1?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, number 1. And this is approximately where Podravanje is and number 2. This route takes you back via Jadar, to Srebrenica and Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And does that X, where that red X is, does that signify anything?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: That's a mistake. When we were marking this yesterday, we made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Nedjelkovic. Do you recall which --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Usher, if we could hold that up there for one minute. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, do you recall now which of those two routes, as you've explained, which of those you took from -- on that day which you took from Bratunac to the mines and which one you took from the mines back to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: We took one or the other route, but I couldn't tell you which one. But one or the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. For both going there -- going to the bauxite mines and coming back, you took one of those two routes or for each leg going to the bauxite mines, firstly. And then secondly coming back you took one of those routes? I'm not sure if I'm --

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I understood you. I think we used both routes, but I am not positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Nedjelkovic, in the days following the fall of Srebrenica, did you see any buses in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: One day I saw a few buses passing by when I was going from my home. And I saw those few buses passing by.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you know where in Bratunac those buses were?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: They were running along the road in the direction of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you recall when this was more precisely, which day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It was after the fall of Srebrenica, maybe two days after that. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did you know where those buses were headed?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I heard that they were headed towards Kladanj. I just heard it on the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did you see who was in those buses?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: There was civilians, women and children. I didn't pay much attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And where -- when you say "they were running along the road in the direction of Konjevic Polje," which road was that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: As I told you, when I turned from my house I took the main street, and that is where I saw these couple of buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And how far is your house from the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: It's not far from the brigade headquarters. It took about a couple of minutes or five minutes walking distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- can you approximate the distance of that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly, but as I told you, when you took a shortcut from the brigade headquarters to the centre, it was between 300 and 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's time for a break. Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in light of the direct and in light of the gentleman's answers, this witness calls for no re-cross -- no cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. This witness is unrelated to the events that took place in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. But anyway, we have to take a break at this moment. We'll resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this stage Judge Argibay has some questions to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. I wanted to ask you two questions. The first one is: You mentioned --

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: You mentioned the playground in Srebrenica. Can you tell us: Where is the playground in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: It is below the town when you cross over the hill of Sase about 1 kilometre below the town, 1 and a half kilometres. I can't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: And the second question is: How far is the place where Mr. Blagojevic's mother lived from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: From Bratunac, well between 7 and 10 kilometres. I can't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Can you repeat the name of the place.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Krasno Polje or Osamsko [phoen]. I think that Osamsko is the village and Krasno Polje is a hamlet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Thank you, I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any questions out of Judge's questions? Yes, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just to clarify one point out of Judge Argibay's questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, you were describing the playground near Srebrenica. When you indicate that -- when you indicate that it was below Srebrenica, was it on the Bratunac side of Srebrenica or on the other side of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: On the side. It is the so-called zero or towards Solocusa [phoen]. If it is easier for you to understand. This residential area is called Vidikovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Perhaps if I could put my question a different way: Is it -- is the playground north or south of Srebrenica town?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Shall I show it to you on the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, if it would be easier, perhaps you could just point to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If the usher could please assist him in going back to the first map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you go down -- so going down from Zalazje and we reached the road that goes to the right to Bratunac and to the left to Srebrenica, this is where the playground is. I hope it's clear for you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And perhaps if the -- if Mr. Usher could assist in providing a blue marker to Mr. Nedjelkovic, he could just --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, if you could please just circle that area where you're indicating the playground to be.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, while you're still standing, could you indicate where the village that you had indicated Mr. Blagojevic's mother was, is that on the map?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me see if I can find my way around this map. Somewhere here by the river Drina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Can you be more specific than that or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah, there it is. Krasno Polje, in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Would you please circle that with a green marker.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Actually, I'm sorry, Mr. Usher, if I could ask you to provide the green marker to Mr. Nedjelkovic. And just for the record these are markings being made on P768.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Somewhere around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nedjelkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I guess I do have one or two questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you were asked some questions with respect to the -- the playground that is near Srebrenica, not inside Srebrenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So you don't have to go into Srebrenica to get to the playground?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. You don't have to go that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I have no further questions. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may ask only one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Am I right to say Mr. Blagojevic's native village is opposite Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it to the north from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And the playground, Potocari, is to the south from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President, just one question arising from the questions that were just asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You want to clarify something?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: In this case you are allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, you have indicated in answer to Mr. Karnavas's question that you don't have to go into Srebrenica to get to the playground. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: But as indicated on your map, the map that's currently showing on the -- on that board, when you left Zalazje on the day after Srebrenica fell and then went towards Pribicevac, you -- did you go through Srebrenica town?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may -- and I don't object to the question, but this is -- this goes beyond the essence of Your Honour's question, his question, my question. Now we're getting into a different area. Now it appears that they're attempting to do direct examination all over again. I don't object in principle, but I think if we're going to be sticking to the Rules, let's stick to the Rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Shin, unless you assure me that this question is related to the question about location of that playground, I will not allow you to proceed in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just wanted to clarify that although the playground is not in Srebrenica and that one doesn't have to go to Srebrenica to go to the playground, I did -- wanted to clarify any mis -- some confusion there about whether Srebrenica was gone into -- any confusion that may relate -- arise from that question, and really that's my only question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour. Now they're trying to place him into Srebrenica. Now he did -- he did have an adequate opportunity, an unlimited opportunity to ask those questions on direct examination. And so usually -- the gentleman can correct me if I'm wrong. The witness, that is. The reason that he used near Srebrenica the playground of Srebrenica is because that's an easy way to identify that particular playground. It has a particular name to it. But if -- when we look at his statement, it indicates -- he says: If you know the playground near Srebrenica, then you know exactly the area where we stopped. Now, they've had an opportunity on direct examination to listen to all the questions. Again, I understand he's new to the case, however I think that if we're going to follow the Rules, we follow the Rules. If not, I think latitude must be given to us in these instances and the Court has been rather restrictive, if I could use that word. So again, I would object to any further questioning unless it specifically relates, Mr. President, to the clarification that you've indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I might.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe on the direct exam, Mr. Nedjelkovic did indicate on the map by explaining what the red marking is, the course he's taken. I would submit that this is proper for re-direct because he has indicated that and a question has come up over whether one would have to go to Srebrenica to go to the playground, potentially causing confusion between the map he's indicated where he's gone through Srebrenica and the answer he gave to Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, in this case you're allowed to ask this question, but try to limit the scope of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: My question will be only what was asked, and I'll repeat the question now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic -- I'm sorry, Mr. Nedjelkovic, on the day after the fall of Srebrenica when you travelled, as you indicated on the map you have to your left, when you went from Zalazje to Pribicevac you indicate the road that you took. Does that road show that you went through Srebrenica after you got to Solocusa?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: We returned again to Zalazje and then we went to Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And when you -- as you indicated on that map, you went down to Solocusa and then just to clarify, that map -- you indicated that you go through Srebrenica and then down towards Jadar. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I'm not so sure that the gentleman said that he went through Srebrenica. I don't object if just he wants to go ahead and ask the question: Did you go through Srebrenica on that particular day. And let's just get it over with. And then maybe the follow-up question is: Did you stop in Srebrenica? What if anything did you do in Srebrenica? What did you see? I don't mind that. So we don't need to do this Kabuki dance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think your question is very good. Mr. Shin, just ask a straight question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjelkovic, let me rephrase the question. When you went from Zalazje then to Solocusa and then down towards Jadar, did you go through Srebrenica town as indicated on that map?

utterances.speaker: MILAN NEDJELJKOVIC
utterances.text: We passed through but we didn't stop anywhere, and we went straight to Pribicevac. I think we passed there, but I never stopped in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karnavas, if you have any questions on this issue, you could put --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I think we got finally to where we needed to get to. And I apologise to my colleague if I am giving him a hard time, but we are trying to keep a good record here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. At this stage are there any documents to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We have two maps, one marked P768 and one marked P767, both with markings the witness made on them that we would tender into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. These two documents are admitted into the evidence. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your testimony. The usher will show you out of the room. We all wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I believe we have Mr. Waespi and the witness in the wings, Your Honour. It's a little tight back here, so they'll be coming in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may, while they're coming in, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We were told that this witness would be testifying tomorrow. And so obviously we certainly would like to hear the direct examination. I'm not prepared at this point in time to do the cross-examination, because we didn't bring the documents here that we need for the cross. So again -- and I don't anticipate cross being very long, but we were given representations that the witness would appear on Tuesday as opposed to today. Had we known about this, obviously we would have brought in and been ready. But I assume that they're going to take at least one full session with this witness. So I'm just alerting the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, during the examining of the witness, anything could happen, you know. Sometimes they are very long, expectably long, sometimes they are short. I think that to be a lawyer you have to be very prepared for any situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I am prepared, Your Honour, to commence; that's not a problem. I doubt if I'm prepared to finish this witness. So if the goal is to finish this witness today, I will not be able to accommodate the Trial Chamber. But I am prepared to commence and to do a good hour worth of cross-examination if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- so as I understand that the witness after the next witness will be here on Thursday. Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He -- yes, that witness, Your Honour, we had scheduled for Friday because unfortunately the witness had a -- some complications and couldn't get here until Thursday. The other witness that is the subject of the motion that we were hoping to get, another one of these short kind of witnesses, we were going to try to fill in for Thursday since we had an open day anyway and it was an important witness. I'm getting information by the hour about whether that -- that's now fourth witness will be available Thursday. But we have fair confirmation for a Friday witness, and that we have -- that was something we had mentioned in the papers and I think it was in the letter that we sent out. That person unfortunately wasn't able to get here until Thursday, so we had to schedule him for Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In this way we have plenty of time. Mr. Karnavas, you may begin your cross-examination tomorrow so as to keep your cross-examination in tact. So when we finish the direct examination of this witness, we'll break until tomorrow afternoon. Well, could we have the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Mr. Waespi, I understand that this witness is a protected witness. Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No, he's not, Mr. President. He has indicated yesterday and also today that he does not need any protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I'm sorry, Witness. Would you please make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Can you please state for the record your full name.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Krsto Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And when were you born?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: 18th of January, 1956.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And where was that?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Sikiric, Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, do you remember having met me and an investigator in my office yesterday?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you remember that I told you that you don't need to talk to us if you didn't want?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Because we were giving you the rights as a suspect. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And we also told you that you had the right to have a lawyer present. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And you were fine and said that you wanted to talk to us.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And today in this courtroom, are you also fine with that and you are able to answer our questions?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us please the -- your profession.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I am a driver and an equipment operator.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, for which company do you work?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Do you work currently?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Not at the moment. I'm doing some plywood business now, but I used to be employed before.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And what was that job you did before?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I worked at the zinc and lead mine Sase, Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And in July 1995 did you also work for that company?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I was with the 3rd Battalion assigned as a security structure for the mine. It was a kind of work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And this 3rd Battalion, was it attached to a specific brigade?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was part of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, let's turn to July 1995. Did you exclusively work for the Sase mine company, or were you also given other assignments?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I worked for the mine. I was with the 3rd Battalion. That was the military 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, what kind of vehicle were you operating in those days?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I drove an M-A-N truck. It's a German make, and the registration plate number was ZV20614.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And can you tell us the colour of this truck.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Orange.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And how many wheels did it have?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Ten wheels.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And can you describe the back of it. Did it have sides?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: It's a dump truck, and it has sides and the back side. It was a dump truck. It didn't have any tarpaulin on it. It has a kind of box which is used for dumping.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And how high were these sides?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Up to 80 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, in July 1995 did you receive an assignment to go somewhere to do a work detail?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I was assigned by the mine manager, and these managers were changed frequently, so I was instructed to report to the Bratunac Brigade command, particularly the civilian protection unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And you told us that it was your superior who told you that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: The company director issued an order for all of us to report to this utility company.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, did you see anybody giving the assignment to your superior?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Military police came in a car. We were within the factory compound. We were working on our trucks, maintaining and repairing them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And this factory compound, that was at the Sase mines?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, why do you know that these people that came in a car were military policemen?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: They had camouflage uniforms and belts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So what exactly did your superior tell you and your colleague?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: My colleague and I were told to report to the command of the Bratunac Brigade to report in front of the brigade headquarters in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And I believe you said that there was a colleague with you. Can you tell the Judges who this colleague was.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: My colleague's name was Miodrag Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you know where he is?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: You mean now?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes.
