utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately he died about a year ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, did you and your colleague take your truck with you?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: We started out with two trucks towards the Bratunac Brigade. Normally it takes about a 15 to 20 minutes to get to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And you had described your truck was the truck of Mr. Obrenovic the same or was it different?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: They were the same, except I had a newer truck and he had an older model, but otherwise they were the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Simic. Just going back to the policemen, you mentioned belts. Do you remember the colour of these belts?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: White. The military police had white belts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you recall what time of the day it was that your superior told you to go to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: It was in the morning at around 9.00 or 10.00. I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you remember the day Srebrenica fell?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact day. The 12th or the 13th or maybe the 11th. Two or three days before or after.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, in relation to this day, the day Srebrenica fell, when did you go to the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Two or three days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, tell us what happened when you arrived at the Bratunac Brigade command. Did you talk to anybody there?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: When we arrived there in front of the headquarters of the Bratunac Brigade, there was several other trucks parked there. There was military police there. So my colleague and I lined up in the column. We were told we had to go to Kravica. We didn't know what we were supposed to do there. First we went to tank fuel at the gas station in Bratunac. We had escort -- our column had escort. Then we tanked fuel, came back, and then headed out towards Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Simic. Let me just go back. You told us that you were told you had to go to Kravica. Do you remember who told you that you had to go to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Momir Nikolic was there on behalf of the military police. He had other policemen around him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And you said he was there. So are you saying it was him who gave you the order to go to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Not me personally, but there were several of us there, four or five or six drivers. We were all there together, and he explained that we had to go to Kravica after we had tanked fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: What was he wearing, Mr. Nikolic? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And what were you wearing that day?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: A military uniform as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And Mr. Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Same.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And you mentioned that there were other drivers who were waiting with you. Do you remember what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you exactly. I think they also had it, but I am not positive whether all of them had a military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, you told us that you were going to Kravica and you mentioned that there was an escort. Can you tell the Judges who provided this escort.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Military police escorted us. They rode in front of us and behind us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So are you saying that they had a car in front of you and a car behind you?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you remember the kind of cars they had?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Passenger vehicles. I couldn't tell you the exact make.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, you told us that there were other drivers. Can you tell us where these --

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: What were these drivers or the trucks were from?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, from Bratunac, from various companies in the area, utility companies, and so on. And I think that there was a truck from Zvornik from a utility company there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Can you describe us this truck you mentioned which came from Zvornik from a utility company.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: It was FAP 13, an orange dump truck, or yellow one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Was it orange or yellow?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I think it was yellow.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you remember who was the driver of this truck?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I didn't know the driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I know it's a long time ago, but do you remember what time about you were driving from Bratunac towards Kravica?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, it could have been at around 12.00 or 1.00, 1.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, you told us about the drivers and their trucks. How many trucks were there all together in your column that was driving from Bratunac to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there were five or six trucks in the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, let's go to Kravica. Can you tell us what happened when this column arrived at Kravica.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: When we arrived in Kravica, we got off the main road and drove to the agricultural co-op and we entered the compound. There were two machines parked there. There was some other workers from civilian protection as well, some soldiers. When we entered the compound, we parked the trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, from -- coming from Bratunac towards Kravica, on which side was the compound?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: The agricultural co-op was on the left side, when riding from Bratunac towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If the witness could please be shown Exhibit P678.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you recognise this picture?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this depicts.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: These are the facilities of the agricultural co-op.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And can you tell us from -- so is that the agricultural compound you discussed just a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And the road in the middle of the picture, that's a road from Kravica to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure from which direction do you mean this from? Left to right or vice versa?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let me ask you: From which side did you come?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: From this side.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps if you could use the pointer and use the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could be given a marker. And I don't know which colour Prosecution witnesses use. I guess it may be blue. Can you just draw a line from where you came from when you entered the compound.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you. And perhaps you can indicate with an R the beginning of that line.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, you told us that there were workers from the -- I think civilian protection there.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Can you describe these people to us. What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: They wore blue work clothes. They were somewhat older.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And how many people wore that?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I can't remember, but there were not that many.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And you also mentioned that there were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: There were soldiers, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And who were these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Soldiers. They wore fatigues. They were the soldiers of the Republika Srpska I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, were these the soldiers who had provided escort to the column or were these different ones?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: They were there when we arrived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And what did the escort members do? Did they stay as well or did they leave once you had arrived?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: They remained in the compound of the agricultural co-op.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you remember what they were doing, the military police members?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't. They were there securing the area while we were working.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us, looking at this picture, where the trucks were located, the trucks you and your colleagues were driving.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: They were here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And perhaps if you could again use the blue pen and make a line.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And please to the middle of those two lines you could indicate the location with a letter T.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now, Mr. Simic, can you tell us what happened next?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: What happened next was that there was a loader there and the people who were in front of me started loading up bodies, assisted by the workers of the civilian protection. This is how the loading started.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Can you describe the loader to us, please.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: The loader had a large shovel in front of it, four wheels, a cabin.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If the witness could please be shown the Prosecution Exhibit 354, which has been previously admitted. That's the sketch which we kindly were given by the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Looking at this exhibit, you see nine different sketches. Can you tell the Trial Chamber which one of those, if any, this loader resembles most.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So you just pointed to the bottom left picture, and it's called a Utovarivac. That's the loader you saw there?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I believe you mentioned there was a second vehicle on the compound when you came. Can you tell us, using this same picture, which other vehicle you saw.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: It wasn't a vehicle. It was a construction machine.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And the witness just pointed to the picture, top right. And it says in B/C/S, I guess, Bager.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now you told us that the loader was operating. Now, what was this Bager doing?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: It was parked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, who was operating this loader?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: The loader was operated by Radenko Crkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And what did he do with this loader?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: They collected dead bodies, together with the workers of the civilian protection, and they loaded them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And where did they collect these bodies from, and you could use the picture again.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: The witness just pointed to an area where a C has been marked with arrows to the left and to the right in the middle of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you remember who it was who was putting this letter C and the arrows into this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Your question is not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. Do you remember who was making these remarks on this picture there, the C plus the arrows? Who did that? I'm sorry, I'm probably still not clear. Do you remember having talked to investigator Bruce Bursik some time ago?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you remember having been shown this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you remember that you were asked to make certain lines and remarks on it?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And was it you who made this letter C?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Okay. I apologise for this little complicated procedure. Can you tell us the letter B, which we see on the left side, did you also make this mark?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And what were you indicating when you made this mark "B"?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: B means that this is where the truck was when the loading took place, the truck that I drove.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, you told us that Mr. Djurkovic was operating the loader. Did you also operate the loader?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: On that day, yes, I did. I operated it as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And can you tell us who asked you to do that.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I received an order from Momir Nikolic to replace a colleague of mine who couldn't do it any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And who was this colleague of yours?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Radenko Djurkovic. I was to replace him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you know why he couldn't do it any longer?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: How would I know? Perhaps he was tired. He was just mentally overburdened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So for how long did you operate the loader?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I loaded up two or three trucks and then he took over and I had to park my truck and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, when you were operating the loader, can you tell us to which part of the warehouse, of the building, we see on this picture you went to collect the bodies?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Here, here, and here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: The witness pointed to the last opening to the right, the dark spot of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And perhaps you can again mark it with the blue pen, just a big circle around these two openings, the one on the right and the one in the middle you mentioned. Just a big circle around it.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Okay. The witness made two circles and a line connecting them with each other, the C being to the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, let's turn to the opening on the right side. What exactly did you do? Did you enter the building with your loader?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: No. The door was not large enough, so it had to be demolished. The loader couldn't enter the building, just the bucket could go through to a point because the opening needed to be made bigger. And then the workers of the civilian protection brought on the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: How many bodies were you able to put into the bucket of your loader at one time?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: How would I know? They didn't count. Perhaps four or five bodies, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let me go back to your own truck. Do you remember how many bodies were loaded onto your own truck?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, about 20, 21 bodies were brought, not as many bodies were loaded as the capacity allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Can you describe the bodies to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you mean how they looked like? How they were dressed?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Those bodies were dressed in camouflage uniforms and let's say about two in my truck had kind of blue working clothes or -- that resembled civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, you just told us that you were also operating the loader at one time when Mr. Djurkovic couldn't do any more. Did you tell that to Mr. Bursik when he interviewed you a couple of weeks ago?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I didn't mention that to him, because nobody asked me. Nobody reminded me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And just a follow-up of what you said about Mr. Nikolic when you -- he told you to replace Mr. Djurkovic. Where was Nikolic when he told you that?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Shall I show it on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: The witness indicated to an area just left of the letter B and below the signs with the letter T.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could make a little cross there where Mr. Nikolic was standing.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Simic. Now, for how long did this process of loading trucks last?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you mean all trucks or just one truck?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: All trucks.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Between one and a half hours and two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, after a specific truck was filled, did this truck leave or did everybody wait until everything was done?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Yeah, we all waited for all the trucks to be loaded and for us to set off together.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: We were headed towards Bratunac and Kravica, the village of Glogova, and that is where we stopped when we went down the slope. We stopped there because we had military police securing us, and that is where we stopped. That was about 4 or 5 kilometres away, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And you said you went down the slope. On which side of the road was the slope?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: None of that was -- the road that was running downhill. That is what I meant by "slope."

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Perhaps I misunderstood you. Was there a time you left the road, Bratunac/Kravica, and turned away?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. We turned to the right. That's a very sharp curve, about 90 degrees when we reached Kravica [as interpreted], and that is a macadam road which is about 3 to 500 metres long.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: The transcript says that you said: "When we reached Kravica." I believe you said when you reached Glogova. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, Glogova. I didn't say "Kravica." So when we reached Glogova, we left the main road by turning to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And you said you continued for 3 to 500 metres. And what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: The convoy stopped. There was -- there were army people as security there. I don't know exactly what. And we saw that a pit or a grave was dug there. The men who were in front of me started unloading the trucks with the assistance of the civilian protection members. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Can you tell us more about the pit or grave that was dug there. How big was it?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: It was about 50 metres long.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And can you tell us how deep it was.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Approximately 1 and a half metres or 2 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: You mentioned the presence of civilian protection members. Were these the same ones you had seen previously in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I think they were the same ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: You also mentioned that you were again escorted by members of the military police. Did these --

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Did they stay with you at Glogova or did they go away?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: They stayed there with us until the whole process was completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: At that time did you see Mr. Nikolic again?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: He came there to the spot with a group of military policemen and his deputies. I don't know. I couldn't recognise any of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Was your truck unloaded as well there?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you remember the time of the day that that happened, your truck was unloaded?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: It was dusk. It wasn't dark yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Did you have to use the headlights of your truck?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: It wasn't necessary to use them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, coming back to the grave, in relation to the macadam road, on which side was the grave?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: On the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, if the witness could be shown the next exhibit, and this is Prosecution Exhibit 679.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you recognise this picture?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And what does it show?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: It shows the road between Kravica and Glogova, and that is where we turned off the road and proceeded for about 500 metres until we reached this spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, can you indicate the spot with a big cross, please.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Where the grave was or something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, please, where the grave was.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And the witness has indicated that he came from the left side, along that big road, and turned into a smaller road where we see this smaller box at the crossroad. And then he went towards the middle of the picture, where he indicated the grave was. And he marked a cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, how long did it last until all the trucks were unloaded?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. I don't think that we stayed more than one hour, about one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Did you stay in your cabin all the time, or did you leave it?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I didn't leave my truck. I sat there all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, after the trucks were unloaded, what happened?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: We unloaded the trucks, and then we headed towards Bratunac, escorted by the military police. We stopped at a parking place not far away from the command. It used to be a parking place of a company. We parked the trucks there. A water tank came. We washed the trucks, and then we left. We went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you know whose water tank that was?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean truck. Truck water tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I am informed, Your Honour, that perhaps that have a segment of his previous answer with respect to where he parked the truck and the location of the brigade that wasn't translated. So perhaps if he could be asked to answer the question again. But I'm told that perhaps the interpreter didn't pick it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, to make the matters more clear, Mr. Waespi, would you please repeat your question so that to give the witness an opportunity to answer it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Witness, can you again repeat the location where you parked the -- your truck.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I parked my truck there on the place that used to be the parking lot of Vihor Bratunac shipping company. And it is about 1.000 metres far from the headquarters. The place is called Borkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you. And perhaps the last question before the break: The water tank, do you know whose water tank that was?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: It belonged to the Bratunac fire brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think that's a convenient moment to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, can I ask how long your direct examination will last?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Not very long, Mr. President. 20 minutes, quarter of an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Shall we finish your direct examination, then we call it a day, because we have already promised Mr. Karnavas they could do their cross-examination tomorrow afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Simic, what did you do the next few days?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I was engaged in Srebrenica for the next few days in cleaning the town. It was very dirty. There was a lot of rubbish and litter and waste, you name it. The town was completely dirty.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And who told you to go there and clean the town?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: The people from my company told me to report to the civilian protection and that we should all go and clean the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Simic. Now, let me turn back to these graves at Glogova. A few months later, were you again concerned with a work detail in relation to these bodies?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: After we had cleaned the town from all the garbage, a few months later - I can't remember exactly - the same thing happened. We received a call from the command. My company ordered me to report to the Bratunac Brigade, and my colleague and I went there with the same trucks. We arrived in front of the Bratunac Brigade headquarters where another couple of trucks were there. There was -- were also military police there and Mr. Nikolic was there. The military police escorted us to the petrol pump in Bratunac to tank our trucks. And we headed again towards Glogova, where we had been previously. We were awaited there by an excavator loader. And I -- it must have been the same one that was used before. It was dark, and the visibility was poor. We stopped there. We -- the whole area was secured, and we started loading again with the backhoe. The military police was there. It was dark when we set off towards Bratunac and Potocari and Srebrenica. And we stopped in Zeleni Jadar. Upon our arrival at Zeleni Jadar, a machine - I think it was a loader but a smaller one - was there. We stopped there, and we saw that there were two graves. I can't describe the shape and the size of the graves for you because it was dark. And we unloaded the bodies that were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Simic. Just a couple of questions to clarify. You said that at Glogova there was an excavator loader. If you could, please refer again to the exhibit you have been shown previously, Exhibit P354. Can you tell us which excavator/loader was operating at Glogova at that time.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: This was the backhoe/excavator, and this -- the one in the bottom left corner was the loader/excavator.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So were --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: The witness pointed at the top middle picture and also at the bottom left one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Did you see both machines operating in Glogova at that time?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. However, the one on the top in the middle was more busy, so to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, do you know who was the operator of these two machines? Do you remember anybody?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I can't remember the person exactly, but the other excavator was operated by Djurkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, for how long did this process of loading the bodies on to the trucks last that evening?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: It lasted for about one and a half hours or two hours. It was dark and we couldn't see very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you remember: Were just the bodies taken out or was it a mixture of bodies and soil?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: There were bodies mixed or not mixed with soil. It depended how the excavator managed to handle the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, perhaps you have told us already, but can you tell us on that day how many trucks you were -- who were operating between Glogova and Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Four or five trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you remember: Were these the same trucks which you had seen a few months before?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: It must have been the case, except for one. And that one was from the Srebrenica express company instead of the one that previously used to be from Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, I think you told us it was dark or it was evening. Can you confirm that, what day -- what time of the day it was.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: It was between 7.00 and 8.00 p.m. when we reached Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, you told us that in Zeleni Jadar you dumped the bodies. Did you see a grave there?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, one couldn't see it clearly because it was dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So you cannot tell the Trial Chamber how big it was?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: No, I cannot because it was dark and one couldn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you know whether there was a machine there who was operating, providing assistance?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: There was a smaller loader than the one that was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And if you could please again tell the Trial Chamber, using the Exhibit 354.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: It was a smaller machine than this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't pick it up. To which picture did you point to?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: The witness pointed to the bottom left picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you know who the driver was of that?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It was dark. I couldn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, during that evening, either at Glogova or at Zeleni Jadar or at both places, did you see Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: Not that I remember. Maybe he may have come. It was dark, but I personally didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, what happened after you finished the unloading?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: We went back towards Srebrenica and Bratunac. And we parked the trucks on the same parking place where they had been before. A water cistern arrived and we washed the trucks again. And then we all went home to bed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Just a couple of more questions, Mr. Simic. You told us that Mr. Djurkovic couldn't finish his job as a loader operator. How did you feel personally about that, what you were doing?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, objection. Relevance. Particularly in light of the fact that the gentleman is a suspect and may not realise the consequences of his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I don't think so. I think this Bench would like to hear the feelings of this witness on this particular issue. Witness, you may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, can you tell the Trial Chamber how you felt that day when you loaded the bodies.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: I felt terribly frightened psychologically, because perhaps this very same loader could have buried my very same relatives during the war in Bratunac. So I didn't -- it was very difficult for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what happened to your relatives.

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: On the 14th of December, 1992, we were attacked by the enemy from Srebrenica so that both my village and Bijelovac Sikiric villages -- village left with only a few survivals who -- all the others were either wounded or killed. On that day, it's a little bit difficult for me to reminisce on this now. I lost my 30-year-old brother. He had 50 wounds in his body. He was massacred, slaughtered. I lost my mother, too. And our other relatives were so mutilated that we could hardly recognise them. Our houses were destroyed or burned and -- I don't wish to talk about it anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let me just finish with one more question. Did anybody from the civilian or military police question you in relation to these events in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: KRSTO SIMIC
utterances.text: No, nobody did, up until a few days ago when your colleague did, the one who came to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: That's it, Mr. President. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you. Thank you, Witness. I'm afraid you have to stay here for one more night, and we'll continue tomorrow afternoon with the cross-examination by the Defence team. So during your stay here in The Hague, you have to remember that you are still under the oath. So do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Have a good rest. Well, we'll resume tomorrow afternoon at 2.15 in the same courtroom

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
